headlines.article_text: Widespread Microsoft outage takes down Outlook and other 365 services Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A Microsoft outage on Thursday and Friday affected users of services like Outlook, Teams and 365. The company said it did not suspect malicious activity was the cause and it was attempting to restore operations. Amazon Web Services said it was "operating normally" and noted inaccurate reports of outages on its platforms. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters Microsoft suffered a widespread outage on Thursday and Friday that impacted users around the world. The outage began shortly before 1 p.m. ET on Thursday and continued into Friday, with Outlook and Teams, along with multiple Microsoft 365 services such as Sharepoint and Copilot, affected. External services that connect with Outlook features such as Calendar also experienced issues. Email and other tools were unavailable for Microsoft users through much of the Asian business day and into the early European hours. In an update just before 7:30 a.m . in London (2:30 a.m. ET), Microsoft said users may still be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook on either web or desktop. It did not give a timeline for restoring full service but said it was seeing "positive results for server stability" after applying a new patch fix to some infrastructure. "As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident. We will continue to treat this incident with urgency and priority until full resolution," Microsoft said, adding that it would provide a full report with further details once the problem was mitigated. Governments and businesses review impact It added it was also adding more computing capacity through virtual machines, software-based servers that run on physical hardware. Governments and businesses in Asia-Pacific and Europe said they were monitoring the situation, which was causing widespread disruption. Earnings for Swiss luxury goods giant Richemont were slightly delayed on Friday due to the outage. Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on Nov. 12, rescheduled the release to Nov. 16, citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage. Air India said it had "temporarily rerouted" emails so it could continue to receive customer messages, adding that its flight operations were not affected. Australian Home Affairs and Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said in a press conference that Microsoft "believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry," Reuters reported. A fault with an update issued by cybersecurity company CrowdStrike caused one of the world's biggest IT system outages in 2024 , hitting airlines, banks and more, Microsoft reported in 2025 that Copilot, its collection of AI assistants and tools, had more than 100 million monthly active users. Amazon Web Services and Google users also reported outages on the site on Thursday. Amazon wrote on X that services were "operating normally" and an "unrelated disruption elsewhere on the internet is prompting some inaccurate news reports." The company referred users to its health dashboard for "accurate data." At 4 p.m. ET Thursday, Microsoft said it had "validated an alternative service health check method" that brought some affected servers back online. "We're now applying this change more broadly," Microsoft wrote. "We're also preparing automated recovery systems to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to maintain service stability while this change progresses." Microsoft initially said infrastructure "elevated load across multiple regions" was responsible for the connectivity problems. The company later determined that the elevated load was caused by a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure" and that some servers were failing automated health checks. "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service," Microsoft wrote .
